title: Wren and the Bakery
premise: Petra Delacroix ghostwrites memoirs for a living, erasing herself from every story she tells — including the secret memoir of celebrity baker Theo Marchand, her rival's biggest client. When a family reunion threatens to expose how far her life has unraveled, she hires a stranger, Wren, to pose as her partner for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but Wren turns out to be the estranged sibling whose inheritance dispute is the very scandal Petra's client wants buried in the memoir. As deadline and reunion collide, Petra must choose between publishing the book that will finally pay off her debts and protecting Wren — and in the end she burns the manuscript, confesses everything, and builds something small and honest of her own beside Wren at a bakery counter.
about_author: Ada Ashgrove spent a decade writing other people's love stories before claiming one of her own; she now lives above a bakery whose croissants she refuses to review. Wren and the Bakery is her first novel under her own name.

chapters.title: The Ghost in Chapter One
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She finishes ghostwriting a bestselling romance while her own savings account hits zero, then receives the contract that could save her: the memoir of celebrity baker Theo Marchand. Emotional beat: weary competence masking quiet desperation.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her mother calls: the annual Delacroix reunion, where relatives measure worth in marriages and mortgages. Petra lies that she's seeing someone. Beat: shame sharpening into recklessness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at Table Nine
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At a café she notices Wren, a quiet pastry cook sketching lamination diagrams, and impulsively offers money for one weekend of pretending. Wren hesitates, then names a price. Beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They meet to build a believable history over flour-dusted counters; Wren insists on real details because 'lies need anchors.' Petra finds herself telling a true story for once. Beat: unexpected intimacy.

chapters.title: The Delacroix Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The performance begins — matching sweaters, invented anniversary — and Petra's family swallows it whole, even warming to Wren. Beat: the strange ache of being believed.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Wren brings a homemade tart that disarms Petra's sharpest aunt; afterward, on the porch, the fake couple forgets to stop holding hands. Beat: the moment pretending stops being pretend.

chapters.title: Payment Declined
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Petra tries to pay; Wren refuses, saying the weekend was real for them. Petra panics and retreats into work. Beat: fear dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Marchand File
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Interviewing Theo, she discovers the memoir's centerpiece: a bitter lawsuit against his estranged sibling who claims half the original bakery. The sibling's name is Wren Ashgrove. Beat: cold dread.

chapters.title: What the Flour Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapter: childhood in the bakery, the father's death, Theo's takeover, the betrayal that made Wren leave. Beat: grief given shape and texture.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Lie
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Wren asks her out properly; Petra accepts, now hiding what she knows. Every tender moment doubles as espionage. Beat: sweetness laced with guilt.

chapters.title: Deadline Pressure
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her publisher moves up the manuscript date; the advance would clear her debts entirely. Theo hints he expects 'the whole ugly truth' about his sibling. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Breadcrumbs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren begins suspecting Petra's questions about the bakery aren't casual; a found draft page confirms someone is writing Theo's story. Beat: trust cracking.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren confronts Petra in the empty kitchen; Petra admits the ghostwriting but not the memoir's contents. Wren walks out. Beat: heartbreak as consequence, not villainy.

chapters.title: Theo's Version
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Theo shares his side — persuasive, wounded, possibly self-serving. Petra realizes both siblings are unreliable narrators of the same wound. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Family Finds Out
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A cousin exposes that the boyfriend was hired; the reunion humiliation Petra feared arrives anyway — but her mother defends her choice to try. Beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Manuscript of Record
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She finishes the memoir and reads the final chapter aloud to an empty room, hearing how cruelly it uses Wren. Beat: the career that saved everything suddenly costs too much.

chapters.title: What Wren Bakes at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sleepless, Wren recreates their father's lost recipe and admits the bakery was never about money — it was about being remembered. Beat: longing transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Climax part one: Petra submits a rewritten final chapter omitting the lawsuit — or burns the draft entirely, forfeiting the advance — and sends Theo her resignation along with the truth. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Counter
chapters.summary: Climax part two, alternating POV. Theo publishes anyway from his own notes; Wren learns Petra sacrificed the advance before learning of the leak. Public fallout forces the siblings into the same room. Beat: collision of all debts.

chapters.title: Siblings, Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren and Theo argue through a night of baking, trading versions of their father until grief becomes shared instead of weaponized. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra arrives to apologize without asking forgiveness; Wren offers not absolution but an invitation — help reopen the old bakery under both names. Beat: second chances earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Wren and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Months later: the reopened shop, Petra writing her own bylined book, Wren's name back on the window. At the reunion they return together, un-hired. Beat: belonging, at last, on honest terms.
